evidence: CAD Macro polarity changes PIT vs revised: 53/200 = 26.5%.
EUR partial Macro polarity changes PIT vs revised: 41/129 = 31.78%.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: Revised historical data can materially alter the state the model would appear to have seen in real time. Revised history is therefore benchmark-only, not true PIT validation.

evidence: CAD hard opposite polarity reversals: 9/200 = 4.5% of all checkpoints.
Most CAD polarity changes occur across the neutral boundary rather than direct +1 to -1 or -1 to +1 reversals.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: Revision sensitivity is concentrated around regime boundaries and confidence transitions more than wholesale opposite-regime rewrites.

evidence: CAD macro flips attributable to Growth-only: 26/53 = 49.06%; Labour-only: 12/53 = 22.64%; both: 15/53 = 28.30%.
EUR macro flips attributable to Growth-only: 19/41 = 46.34%; Labour-only: 11/41 = 26.83%; both: 11/41 = 26.83%.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: Growth is the larger revision-sensitive block in both available two-block PIT samples, but this does not justify reweighting without forward evidence.

evidence: GDP direction changes: 19/68 = 27.94%.
Retail direction changes: 18/68 = 26.47%.
Retail turning changes: 20/68 = 29.41%.
Unemployment direction changes: 12/69 = 17.39%.
Employment direction changes: 10/69 = 14.49%.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: GDP direction and Retail turning behavior are the largest observed CAD series-level revision sensitivities.

evidence: CAD first-release GDP/Retail divergence: 40/135 = 29.63%.
Growth block direction changes when divergent: 19/40 = 47.5% versus 23/95 = 24.21% when aligned.
Near-threshold divergent cases: 24/40 = 60%.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: Internal Growth disagreement is associated with materially higher revision fragility and lower conviction. It is a future confidence-modifier candidate, not a current engine rule.

evidence: Employment/Unemployment divergence: 9/69 = 13.04%.
Labour block direction changes when divergent: 2/9 = 22.22% versus 12/60 = 20.0% when aligned.
Near-threshold divergent cases: 8/9 = 88.89%.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: Labour internal divergence is mainly a low-conviction marker in this sample, not a clear amplifier of direction revision fragility.

evidence: Growth-only fragile checkpoints produce Macro polarity flips in 26/43 = 60.47%.
Labour-only fragile checkpoints produce Macro polarity flips in 12/20 = 60.0%.
Both-block fragile checkpoints produce Macro polarity flips in 15/22 = 68.18%.
Neither block direction fragile: 0/115 Macro polarity flips.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: When block direction itself changes PIT vs revised, the revision often propagates into overall Macro. When neither block direction changes, Macro polarity is stable in the CAD sample.

evidence: CAD turning changes: 53/200; 17/115 occur with neither block direction changing.
EUR turning changes: 51/129; 23/51 = 45.10% occur without a Macro polarity flip.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: Turning point should be treated as an early-warning layer rather than the same confidence class as a confirmed Macro direction change.

evidence: CAD persistent turning confirms Macro polarity within two checkpoints in 13/19 = 68.42%.
EUR persistent turning with second checkpoint available confirms within two checkpoints in 16/21 = 76.19%.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: The research hierarchy FIRST SIGNAL -> POSSIBLE CHANGE -> CONFIRMED STRUCTURAL CHANGE is supported across CAD and EUR, but remains a descriptive validation hierarchy until forward OOS evidence exists.

evidence: USD eligible PIT series pass release-date chronology checks.
EUR eligible PIT series pass release-date chronology checks.
CAD aggregate forward-filled source checkpoints are never later than the aggregate checkpoint.
Replay availability filter is release_date <= checkpoint and does not use observation date as an as-of gate.
methodology_conclusions.interpretation: No lookahead leakage was detected in the currently eligible PIT replay at daily-date resolution.

evidence_limits: CAD is the only G8 currency with a full Growth+Labour PIT core in this validation set.
EUR has both blocks but partial series coverage because Retail volume and negotiated wages are withheld.
USD has PIT Growth only and cannot produce a complete historical Macro polarity vote.
GBP, JPY, CHF, AUD and NZD historical Macro remain WITHHELD under PIT rules.
Cross-country turning conclusions currently rest on CAD and EUR only and must not be generalized mechanically to the full G8.
Daily-date lookahead checks do not validate intraday timestamps.

forward_oos.note: No parameter tuning or engine-rule promotion should occur from partial PIT evidence before forward OOS checkpoints are evaluated.

next_action: Wait for canonical forward OOS checkpoints while limiting interim work to validation-only, data-integrity, presentation, or non-engine operational tasks that do not contaminate the frozen OOS.
